name: Sovereign Software Evaluation Framework
policyNote: This is an evidence-led evaluation framework. It adopts no weighting scheme, numerical score, or tier threshold, and it is not an externally accredited certification scheme.

principles.name: Sovereignty
principles.definition: Users retain meaningful control of their data, essential capabilities, and ability to leave or replace providers. Sovereignty requires practical, not merely contractual, authority over one's records and essential workflows.
principles.question: If the vendor changed its rules tomorrow, would the user still hold meaningful authority over their work?

levels.meets: Users can access, export, back up, restore, and migrate their information through documented means, and no revocable vendor decision removes their essential capabilities.
levels.partial: Exit and access are possible but incomplete, costly, or dependent on undocumented steps, or some essential capability remains subject to vendor permission.
levels.does_not_meet: Essential information or functions can be withdrawn by a vendor, with no practical way to leave without unacceptable loss.

principles.improvement: Document a complete export and migration path, remove revocable vendor control over essential functions, and explain key custody and recovery honestly.

home.title: Sovereignty: The User Is the Authority
home.short: Users retain meaningful control of their data, essential capabilities, and ability to leave or replace providers.
home.text: An individual or organization should not lose access to essential information merely because a subscription expires, an identity provider changes its rules, or a service is discontinued. Sovereignty requires practical, not merely contractual, authority: users can access, export, back up, restore, and migrate their information through documented means. A managed service can respect sovereignty if meaningful exit and independent access remain available, and local installation alone proves nothing if essential functions can be revoked remotely.
home.takeaway: The ability to leave without losing what is yours is a practical test of ownership.

principles.name: Longevity
principles.definition: Records and intellectual work remain accessible, interpretable, and recoverable after applications, vendors, and runtimes disappear. Preserving bytes is insufficient if their meaning, relationships, or means of recovery disappear.
principles.question: Will the user's information remain understandable and recoverable after the original software is gone?

levels.meets: Records and their meaning can be preserved, interpreted, and restored by an independent party, with documented formats and tested recovery.
levels.partial: Data can be exported, but documentation, relationships, metadata, or restoration are incomplete or untested.
levels.does_not_meet: Records are held in an undocumented format or system that only the original vendor can interpret or restore.

principles.improvement: Publish format and schema documentation, preserve metadata and relationships in exports, and test backup and restoration regularly.

home.title: Longevity: Information Should Outlive Software
home.short: Records and intellectual work remain accessible, interpretable, and recoverable after applications, vendors, and runtimes disappear.
home.text: Applications are temporary, while research, designs, records, and creative work may matter for generations. Longevity has three dimensions: data (records and metadata can be preserved and restored independently), function (essential workflows can continue through maintained software, independent implementations, or practicable migration), and knowledge (formats, schemas, and recovery procedures are documented well enough for future people and tools). A documented binary format such as SQLite can qualify, but open format names alone guarantee nothing.
home.takeaway: Applications are temporary. Human information deserves a longer life.

principles.name: Locality
principles.relationship: Locality provides a powerful means of independence.
principles.definition: Capabilities that can reasonably operate on user-controlled hardware do not depend unnecessarily on continuous external connectivity or permission.
principles.question: Which essential functions keep working without remote permission, and are the remaining dependencies genuinely necessary and replaceable?
evidence: Which essential functions operate without remote permission
Which dependencies are genuinely necessary and replaceable

levels.meets: Everything that can reasonably work on the user's hardware does, and remaining network dependencies are inherent to the task and replaceable.
levels.partial: Core work is possible without the network, but some dependencies are imposed by business or architectural choices or cannot be substituted.
levels.does_not_meet: Reading, creating, or searching the user's own work requires someone else's permission or connectivity without a reason inherent to the task.

principles.improvement: Move work that can run locally onto user-controlled hardware, make synchronization optional and replaceable, and explain which dependencies are inherent to the task.

home.title: Locality: Independence by Design
home.short: Capabilities that can reasonably operate on user-controlled hardware do not depend unnecessarily on external connectivity or permission.
home.text: The network should extend what software can do, not arbitrarily determine whether a person can reach work already on their device. Where technically appropriate, reading, editing, searching, and essential calculation should stay available on hardware the user controls, and a failed synchronization should not erase the ability to work. Locality is not an absolutist offline demand: the question is whether a dependency is inherent to the task and replaceable, or imposed unnecessarily. Local data also needs credible backups and recovery paths.
home.takeaway: If a task can reasonably be performed independently, its execution should not require someone else's permission.

principles.name: Transparency and Control
principles.relationship: Transparency and Control make authority meaningful in operation.
principles.definition: Users can understand, inspect, authorize, and, where feasible, reverse or contest significant actions taken on their behalf.
principles.question: Can a person understand, authorize, and correct what the software does that matters?

levels.meets: Important operations follow explained rules, material changes are traceable, suggestions are distinct from committed actions, and users can approve, reverse, or contest outcomes appropriate to the risk.
levels.partial: Rules or effects are partly documented or visible, but some consequential behavior cannot be inspected, authorized, or corrected.
levels.does_not_meet: Significant actions happen without visibility, authorization, or recourse.

principles.improvement: Explain the rules behind important operations, make consequential changes traceable, separate suggestions from committed actions, and give users a way to approve, reverse, or contest outcomes.

home.title: Transparency and Control: Authority Must Be Exercisable
home.short: Users can understand, inspect, authorize, and, where feasible, reverse or contest significant actions taken on their behalf.
home.text: A person cannot meaningfully govern a tool whose consequential behavior is inscrutable. Sovereign Software explains the rules governing important operations, reveals relevant dependencies and data flows, makes material changes traceable, and distinguishes suggestions from committed actions. Determinism is often the right engineering mechanism, but it is not itself the principle: a deterministic black box can still deny control, while a system that uses statistical models can remain governable when its boundaries and effects are transparent.
home.takeaway: The machine may assist in decisions; it must not quietly take ownership of them.

eligibility.title: Independent access to essential information
eligibility.failure: The user cannot obtain an intelligible copy of already-created essential records through a documented, workable process.
eligibility.question: Can the user obtain an intelligible copy of already-created essential records using a documented, workable process?

eligibility.title: Practicable exit and migration
eligibility.failure: The user cannot leave for an alternative workflow without unacceptable loss of essential information and meaning.
eligibility.question: Can the user leave for an alternative workflow or implementation without unacceptable loss of essential information and meaning?

eligibility.title: Independent interpretation and recovery
eligibility.failure: Preserved records cannot be interpreted or meaningfully restored without an irreplaceable vendor-controlled system.
eligibility.question: Can preserved records be interpreted and meaningfully restored without an irreplaceable vendor-controlled system?

eligibility.title: Continuing authority and custody over already-created work
eligibility.failure: Withdrawal of permission, payment, activation, or provider availability removes effective control or essential operations over existing work, or architectural custody defects expose confidential records to unauthorized parties by design.
eligibility.question: If new permission, payment, activation, or provider availability is withdrawn, can the user still retain effective custody and continue essential operations over existing work without architectural exposure to unauthorized parties?

eligibility.title: Governability of consequential actions
eligibility.failure: Consequential operations cannot be adequately authorized, inspected, or corrected or contested where feasible, given the risks of this software.
eligibility.question: For the risks of this software, can consequential operations be adequately authorized, inspected, and corrected or contested where feasible?

tests.title: Ownership and exit
tests.question: Can essential information be accessed, exported, and migrated independently?
verify: Key custody and recovery explained, where applicable

tests.title: Preservation and recovery
tests.question: Can an independent party interpret and restore the important records?

tests.title: Offline independence
tests.question: Which functions continue when external services are unavailable, and why?
verify: Functions that continue without external services
Each remaining dependency shown to be inherent to the task and replaceable
A failed synchronization does not remove the ability to work

tests.title: Operational transparency and control
tests.question: Can consequential actions, permissions, dependencies, and outcomes be inspected and controlled?
verify: Rules for important operations are explained
Consequential actions and outcomes are traceable
Suggestions are distinct from committed actions
Approval, reversal, or contest is available where appropriate

tests.title: Security, custody, and continuity
tests.question: Are custody, encryption, backups, restoration, and vendor-failure scenarios credibly addressed?
verify: Custody of data and keys against unauthorized parties

tests.title: Interoperability and maintainability
tests.question: Do interfaces, formats, and architectural boundaries materially support freedom and long-term operation?

tests.title: Human experience and performance
tests.question: Is the software usable, accessible, and reasonably responsive for its domain?

labels.does_not_meet_core: Does not meet the proposed core standard

evidence.note: A determination needs a recorded observation for every principle finding and for every requirement marked Pass, a written justification for every Not Applicable, and no Low or unstated confidence on a principle finding. Low confidence alone cannot establish a Pass or a Fail.
